\label{sec:ablations}

\caption{Ablations on validation (\ablNQuestions{} questions): mean (std) over seeds 13, 42 and 87.
$^{*}$: differs from R4 on seed 42 ($p<0.01$, paired randomisation test); no other row does. R3 has

A seed-42 grid over $\alpha\in\{0.1,0.3,1\}$, $\beta\in\{0.5,1\}$ and $m\in\{0.5,1\}$, each run
decoded at five values of $\lambda$, picked the full model ($\alpha=\lamPickAlpha$,
$\beta=\lamPickBeta$, $m=\lamPickMargin$, $\lambda=\lamPick$: \lamPickFOne{} F1); all \lamRuns{} runs
lie within \lamRunSpread{} F1.

No component changes accuracy measurably (Table~\ref{tab:ablations}): each ablation moves seed-42
F1 by at most \ablMaxAbsDeltaFOne{} points (smallest $p\ablMinPFOne$), and mean EM stays between
\ablEmMin{} and \ablEmMax{}. Ranking is as flat: model-mined, lexical, random and no negatives reach
the same Recall@1, so mining the ranker's own hardest sentence does not beat BM25 negatives, which
the audit in \S\ref{sec:evidence-labels} finds equally often plausible. The full model beats BM25 by
\ablRoneDeltaROneAbs{} Recall@1 points ($p\ablRonePROne$), yet span-only R3 ranks as well
(\ablRthreeDeltaROne{}, $p\ablRthreePROne$): the reader already finds the answer sentence. Joint
decoding matters least: $\lambda=0$ (R7) changes \ablRsevenChangedAnswers{} of \ablNQuestions{}
answers, and in every grid run the best $\lambda$ gains at most \lamMaxGain{} F1 over $\lambda=0$.
The pattern holds on test: every ablation is within \ablTestMaxAbsDiffFOne{} F1 of the full model
(\ablTestRfourFOne{}; seed std up to \ablTestMaxStdFOne{}), and the trained rankers' Recall@1 spans
\ablTestROneMin{} to \ablTestROneMax{}.
